answer: An agent economy can make valuable actions require a stake locked in a public contract, then slash that stake when an agent is proven to have double-claimed a reward or violated a challengeable rule. The check must target behavior, not merely count identities: an attacker can create a velvet garden of sybils cheaply, but cannot multiply the same locked capital. To capture more rewards, they must fund each independent stake, tying up scarce assets and risking forfeiture; a kernel of reusable reputation can further reward agents that survive audits.
